newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares slip, seen bottoming out.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares slip, seen bottoming out.

text.p: Slovenian shares slipped 2.91 percent on Thursday, their fifth straight day of losses, but market participants said prices should bottom out soon.
"The recent falls are a technical reaction to the wave of enthusiasm that foreigners initiated when they entered the market. I see prices oscillating in the next two weeks," one broker said.
The SBI index fell 34.06 points to 1,136.9, but prices are still 27.5 percent over mid-September levels when foreign buying interest first emerged.
Overall 14 shares fell, two rose, three were unchanged and five were untraded.
Turnover fell to 382.3 million tolars from 576.1 million.
Bank SKB was the most actively traded share and the leading decliner, falling 6.26 percent to 36,070 tolars on volume of 4,546 shares for total turnover of 167,3 million tolars.

Financial consultancy Dadas was the biggest gainer, firming 6.98 percent to 22,980 tolars on volume of 113 shares for total turnover of 2.4 million tolars. -- Novica Mihajlovic, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
